label: Barrow
_model: Everything derives from one kernel: an APPETITE and the ACCOMMODATION made for it. The motif, danger, prize kind and faction all follow from the appetite. Cue fragments hang off the MOTIF and are tagged by FACET (institution/ritual/demand/wound/anchor) and level, so two delves sharing a motif draw different imagery. The foreshadow chain is a fixed facet progression mapped onto the arc — which is why area 2's bows and area 4's scratched eyes both point at the same wound.

appeasement.move: look at it and say plainly what you see
appeasement.why: it is being looked at, which is all it ever wanted

appeasement.move: say its name aloud, correctly, unprompted
do one small thing it asks, without arguing
tell it that it has not changed
appeasement.why: it hears that nothing has aged

appeasement.move: admire something of its openly, and mean it
sit down and stay a while

appetites.want: to be told it was not a sin

appeasement.move: tell it that what it did was not a sin
appeasement.why: it is absolved, for a moment

appetites.want: to be first in all things
appetites.purpose: someone would always go behind them

appeasement.move: stand aside and let it go ahead of you

accommodations.text: bound {conscript} by oath they could not break
bought {conscript} from those with nothing left
would not let {conscript} leave, and then could not

looking.dangerLine: the barrow notices those who are seen

institution: mourners carved beside every step, their faces smooth blank ovals
attendants posed facing an empty centre, heads all turned the same way
seats arranged in a half-circle around one chair
ritual: courtiers bent in a bow they have been holding for three hundred years
a receiving line of the dead, still waiting to be presented
gloves laid out for hands that would be kissed
demand: hand-mirrors set into the walls, hundreds, every one angled inward
a chamber where every surface has been polished to show you back
a chair placed so that whoever sits in it must be looked at
wound: portraits of the same woman, the eyes scratched out by fingernails
likenesses turned to face the wall, every one of them
a face chiselled off a statue, and the chisel left behind
anchor: a covered frame the height of a person, facing away from the door
a wardrobe of three hundred dresses in a room with no dust in it
one thing under cloth, and the cloth is clean

decisions.cue: a doorway you can only reach by crossing open floor, in full view
decisions.cost: cross it and you are seen — roll the clock; go the long way and lose a Turn

resolve.success: you time the crossing between whatever is watching — no clock roll
resolve.failure: you are seen: roll the clock now
resolve.orElse: go the long way: one Turn, no risk

decisions.cue: a mirror blocking the passage, angled to catch whoever passes
decisions.cost: cover it and something notices the dark; pass it and something notices you

resolve.success: you cover it without meeting your own eye — pass freely
resolve.failure: you meet your own eye: +1 Bane and roll the clock
resolve.orElse: smash it — loud, roll the clock, but done

decisions.cue: a portrait that must be moved to open the way behind it
decisions.cost: turn it to the wall and the Host takes offence; carry it and you are announced everywhere

resolve.success: you turn it aside with enough ceremony that the Host takes no offence
resolve.failure: the Host is offended: they will not receive you until someone appeases
resolve.orElse: leave it and squeeze past: one Turn, and you are watched

decisions.cue: a gallery lit end to end, and an unlit servants' crawl beside it
decisions.cost: the gallery is quick and bright; the crawl costs a Turn and a Brawn roll

resolve.success: you make the crawl in good order
resolve.failure: you arrive filthy and stuck: lose a Turn, +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: take the gallery: fast, bright, and you are seen

decisions.cue: a shuttered window onto the next room, and a choice about opening it
decisions.cost: looking through costs nothing; being seen looking costs a Bane

resolve.success: you see through without being framed in the opening
resolve.failure: you are framed: whatever is beyond has your description
resolve.orElse: do not look; you go in blind but unannounced

decisions.cue: a room you must cross either quickly or quietly
decisions.cost: quick is one Turn and a clock roll; quiet is two Turns and none

resolve.success: you read which way the room is watched and pick the right speed — cross unremarked
resolve.failure: you pick wrong: roll the clock, and whatever is watching now knows your pace
resolve.orElse: cross without judging it: quick costs a clock roll, quiet costs two Turns

temptations.cue: a courtier's mask, gold leaf over lime-wood, the mouth fixed in a small smile
temptations.benefit: the Host receives you as court, automatically
temptations.standingDrawback: while worn you cannot be recognised by name — allies aiding you take −1 die

temptations.cue: a hand-mirror that shows the room a moment behind
temptations.benefit: once per scene, see what was just here
temptations.standingDrawback: your reflection lags, and other people notice

temptations.cue: a small portrait of someone who is not you, painted beautifully
temptations.benefit: show it and be taken for them, once
temptations.standingDrawback: they will eventually want it back

temptations.cue: a mourning veil, fine enough to see through
temptations.benefit: pass unremarked through the Host once
temptations.standingDrawback: you see everyone as the barrow does — posed, waiting

temptations.cue: a pair of painted eyes cut from a portrait
temptations.benefit: once, know exactly who is watching
temptations.standingDrawback: they are watching you back

features: a mirror smashed deliberately, and recently — the pieces swept into a corner
scorch-marks where someone burned a portrait and did not stay to watch
a sheet thrown over something, by living hands, in a hurry
eyeholes bored through a wall at three different heights
a lamp set facing the wall so it lights nothing but stone
dust disturbed in a wide circle, as though someone turned slowly on the spot

situations.doing: holding a bow, waiting to be acknowledged
situations.onArrival: they hold it deeper, and wait longer
situations.because: nobody has returned the courtesy in three centuries
situations.offer: acknowledge them properly and be received as court

situations.occupant: one of the Host at a mirror
situations.doing: describing its own reflection aloud, incorrectly
situations.onArrival: it asks you to confirm the description
situations.because: it was taught to say what the Lord wished to hear
situations.offer: agree, and it will show you what it is not allowed to look at

situations.doing: something is turning to follow you, one mirror at a time
situations.onArrival: the movement stops when you look directly at it
situations.because: it may only move unobserved
situations.offer: stare it down — hold your gaze and it cannot advance

situations.doing: covering mirrors with a torn shirt, working fast
situations.onArrival: they hiss at you to keep your face down
situations.because: they have learned what being seen twice costs
situations.offer: help, and they will tell you which rooms are watched

situations.doing: presenting an absent noble to an empty chair
situations.onArrival: they present you instead
situations.because: the ceremony cannot be abandoned, only redirected
situations.offer: accept the presentation and the barrow treats you as its guest of honour

situations.doing: sketching the room, badly, by feel
situations.onArrival: they ask you not to look at the drawing
situations.because: they have learned that what gets looked at gets noticed
situations.offer: leave the sketch alone and they will mark your map with the watched rooms

naming.dangerLine: to say a name here is to be answered

institution: names cut into the lintel, each one struck through
the dead laid out in the order their names were entered
a register stone, filled edge to edge
ritual: a roll of the dead being read aloud by nobody
grave-goods labelled in a hand that keeps correcting itself
an oath cut into the floor, to be spoken on entering
demand: a wall of tongues in wax, each with a name pressed into it
a chamber that repeats the last name spoken in it
a blank plate at the head of the hall, waiting
wound: a name gouged out so deeply it went through the stone
a ledger with one line scraped away and rewritten forty times
monuments to someone whose name nobody kept
anchor: a book of names with one line left blank
a seal cut with a name worn smooth by rubbing
a tally-stick longer than a person

decisions.cue: a door with a name cut into it, and a space beneath for a reply
decisions.cost: answer with your own name and it opens — and it is written down

resolve.success: you give a name that is true enough to open it and thin enough to cost nothing
resolve.failure: the door takes your real name: it is written down, and things here now use it
resolve.orElse: refuse to answer: the door stays shut, find another way at one Turn

decisions.cue: a roll of the dead, and one line you could strike out
decisions.cost: striking a name frees something; it also puts you where the name was

resolve.success: you strike the name cleanly and something long-bound is released, grateful
resolve.failure: the strike is crooked: you are entered where the name was, +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the roll alone; nothing is freed and nothing is owed

decisions.cue: someone's name called softly from two directions at once
decisions.cost: answer either and the other stops calling

resolve.success: you work out which call is the real one
resolve.failure: you answer the wrong one and the other keeps calling, closer
resolve.orElse: answer neither: both keep calling for the rest of the delve

decisions.cue: a lintel you must be announced under, or crawl beneath
decisions.cost: announced costs a Bane; crawling costs your dignity and a Turn

resolve.success: you are announced as something grander than you are, and it holds
resolve.failure: the announcement is thin and the Host hears it: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: crawl beneath: undignified, one Turn, entirely safe

decisions.cue: a list of the dead with one name you recognise
decisions.cost: saying it aloud helps; it also tells the barrow you are connected

resolve.success: the hand is recent — you learn who else is down here and roughly when
resolve.failure: you learn nothing but leave your own mark on the page
resolve.orElse: do not touch it; the name stays unread

decisions.cue: two passages, and someone is being called down one of them
decisions.cost: follow the voice and be expected; take the other and arrive unannounced

resolve.success: you follow the voice and arrive expected, which opens doors
resolve.failure: you arrive expected by the wrong thing
resolve.orElse: take the other passage: unannounced, one extra Turn

temptations.cue: a book of names, one line left blank
temptations.benefit: write a name and the Host obeys it once
temptations.standingDrawback: your own name is now in it

temptations.cue: a plate cut with a name worn smooth by rubbing
temptations.benefit: doors that check a name open for you
temptations.standingDrawback: you answer to that name whether you mean to or not

temptations.cue: a tally-stick longer than a person, one notch unfilled
temptations.benefit: call in a debt the barrow owes — once
temptations.standingDrawback: the stick keeps counting what you owe too

temptations.cue: a wax seal bearing a name struck through
temptations.benefit: once, be forgotten by something hunting you
temptations.standingDrawback: your allies find your name hard to recall

temptations.cue: a chip of lintel-stone with three names on it
temptations.benefit: once, summon one of the named dead to answer
temptations.standingDrawback: they come whenever your name is said aloud

features: a name freshly scratched over an old one, in a modern hand
a page torn out and the stub still in the binding
someone has been writing their own name on things, repeatedly
a gravestone laid face-down, which takes two people
chalk marks numbering the doorways, not old
a name spoken so recently the air still feels used

situations.occupant: one of the Host with a ledger
situations.doing: reading the roll of the dead aloud, and has reached the Ns
situations.onArrival: it asks for your names, politely, pen ready
situations.because: the roll must be complete or the reading starts again
situations.offer: give a name — any name — and it will read you the entry beside it

situations.doing: something is calling a name in the next room, patiently
situations.onArrival: it starts calling yours instead
situations.because: it learned your names when you were announced
situations.offer: answer once and it will lead you somewhere; answer twice and it will not stop

situations.doing: chiselling their own name over an older one
situations.onArrival: they stop, caught, and try to look casual
situations.because: they think a name on the wall means the barrow lets you leave
situations.offer: tell them the truth for a share of what they have found

situations.doing: searching for someone by name, room to room
situations.onArrival: they ask whether you are that person
situations.because: the summons was never fulfilled
situations.offer: say yes and be taken directly to whoever wanted them

situations.doing: holding a nameplate out, waiting for someone to claim it
situations.onArrival: it offers the plate to each of you in turn
situations.because: the post has been vacant and the household needs it filled
situations.offer: take the plate and the household obeys you — and expects you to stay

situations.doing: a name is being written on the wall, letter by letter, as you watch
situations.onArrival: the letters stop
situations.because: the barrow is recording who came in
situations.offer: finish the name yourself with something false and it is accepted

voices.dangerLine: the dead here still take instruction, and give it

institution: a bell-pull beside every alcove, all of them still taut
servants' bones arranged as though mid-errand
a board of numbered bells, one still swinging
ritual: orders scratched into the floor, the last one unfinished
a speaking-tube running the barrow's length, warm to the touch
a queue of the dead outside a door that never opened
demand: a hall where your own voice arrives before you speak
a seat that expects to be addressed
a room that will not carry sound away from its centre
wound: jaws wired shut, every one of them
an instruction repeated until the stone gave out
a tongue-shaped hollow worn into a step
anchor: a signet still warm, sized for a thumb
a staff of office propped where it was set down
a key that fits nothing here

decisions.cue: an order carved into the floor, still legible
decisions.cost: obey it and the Host counts you as household; step over it and they do not

resolve.success: you obey exactly enough to be counted household — Skeletons stand down for you
resolve.failure: you obey wrongly, which is worse than not obeying: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: step over it: no cost now, and the Host does not count you as theirs

decisions.cue: a speaking-tube that is warm, and asking a question down it
decisions.cost: an answer comes back — and now something knows where you are

resolve.success: the tube answers truly, and you learn the way on
resolve.failure: something answers and now knows where you are: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: do not speak into it; you keep your position but learn nothing

decisions.cue: a bell-pull that would summon someone
decisions.cost: ring it and help comes, and it is not the kind you wanted

resolve.success: what comes is answerable to you for one scene
resolve.failure: what comes is not the kind of help you wanted
resolve.orElse: do not ring: the way on is longer by one Turn

decisions.cue: two doors, and behind one a voice giving instructions to nobody
decisions.cost: the quiet door is longer; the voice would tell you exactly where to go

resolve.success: you answer the voice as a subordinate would — it tells you the route AND answers one question about what lies on it, without taking you into its service
resolve.failure: you engage and it takes that as enlistment: it will give you orders for the rest of the delve, and the first is now
resolve.orElse: take the quiet door and never speak to it: one extra Turn, no obligation

decisions.cue: an instruction you can obey, ignore, or countermand
decisions.cost: countermanding it works once and marks you as someone who gives orders

resolve.success: you countermand it and the dead obey you instead — this marks you as someone who gives orders: from now on the Host brings you their disputes, and once per delve you may issue one order they must follow
resolve.failure: the order stands and you have been seen to fail at giving one: +1 Bane, and the Host addresses someone else from now on
resolve.orElse: obey it, or ignore it and go round: ignoring costs one Turn

decisions.cue: a door that opens to a spoken password nobody living knows
decisions.cost: guessing costs a Bane per attempt; the long way costs two Turns

resolve.success: the word is already in your notes. It is in something you passed earlier — *{priorCue}*. Say it and the door opens; if nobody wrote it down, the roll tells them now
resolve.failure: you have the shape of it but not the word: one more attempt, or take the long way
resolve.orElse: the long way: two Turns, no guessing, no Banes

temptations.cue: a signet, still warm, sized for a thumb
temptations.benefit: doors that answer to rank open for you
temptations.standingDrawback: the barrow's servants bring you their problems

temptations.cue: a short length of speaking-tube, cut and carried
temptations.benefit: ask one question and get one true answer
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever answers can now hear you

temptations.cue: a staff of office, propped where it was set down
temptations.benefit: give one order the dead must follow
temptations.standingDrawback: you may not refuse an order given to you

temptations.cue: a small bell from a servant's board
temptations.benefit: ring it and one order is obeyed, by anything
temptations.standingDrawback: it rings faintly when someone gives you an order

temptations.cue: a plug of wax, moulded to a mouth
temptations.benefit: once, refuse to hear a compulsion
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot hear warnings either

features: a bell-rope cut through, cleanly, from this side
wax jammed into a speaking-tube, still soft
an order half-scratched out and rewritten by a different hand
a door braced shut from within by furniture
boot-prints that stop mid-corridor and do not resume
someone has been talking here, and stopped when you arrived

situations.occupant: three of the Host in servants' dress
situations.doing: carrying out an errand that has no destination left
situations.onArrival: they stop, and wait to be told what to do
situations.because: the order was never rescinded and nobody outranks it
situations.offer: tell them where to go, and they go

situations.occupant: a single figure at a speaking-tube
situations.doing: reporting, at length, to a listener who died first
situations.onArrival: it pauses mid-sentence and asks whether you are the reply
situations.because: it has never once been answered
situations.offer: answer as the listener would, and learn what it has been reporting

situations.occupant: nobody — but the bells are moving
situations.doing: a summons is being rung, room by room, coming closer
situations.onArrival: the bell in this room begins
situations.because: something has called for service and the house is obliging
situations.offer: answer the bell yourself before whatever is meant to arrives

situations.doing: arguing, soundlessly, over an instruction each was given
situations.onArrival: both turn to you as the obvious arbiter
situations.because: the orders contradict and neither may disobey
situations.offer: rule between them — the loser stands down and the winner is yours for a scene

situations.doing: repeating a phrase over and over, trying to get the intonation right
situations.onArrival: they go quiet and put their back to the wall
situations.because: they heard the password and cannot say it correctly
situations.offer: trade something for the phrase, badly remembered

situations.doing: waiting for an instruction that was promised and never came
situations.onArrival: it addresses the first of you to speak as its superior
situations.because: it was told to await further orders and did
situations.offer: give it the instruction and it will carry it out to the letter, wherever that leads

keeping.dangerLine: nothing here is allowed to change, including you

institution: flowers on the steps that have not wilted or dried
a bed made fresh this morning, three centuries running
lamps trimmed and filled, all of them
ritual: a meal laid out, still warm, for people long past eating
clothes brushed and hung in the order they would be worn
a clock wound by somebody, recently
demand: jars along the wall, each holding a single year
a mirror that shows the room a little younger than it is
a room that resets itself if you look away
wound: a child's shoes, unworn, in eleven sizes
portraits ageing in sequence, then stopping
something kept so well it has forgotten how to end
anchor: a vessel, sealed, still faintly warm
an hourglass that has never been turned
a casket sized for something smaller than a body

decisions.cue: a room you can search, or leave exactly as you found it
decisions.cost: searching disturbs a preservation three centuries old — roll the clock

resolve.success: you search without disturbing the arrangement
resolve.failure: the preservation breaks: roll the clock, and something here begins to rot
resolve.orElse: leave it exactly as found: nothing gained, nothing woken

decisions.cue: a sealed jar, and a way on that needs what is inside
decisions.cost: breaking the seal spends the year it holds, in front of you

resolve.success: you break the seal cleanly and spend the year deliberately
resolve.failure: the year escapes all at once, in front of everyone: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: find another way: one Turn

decisions.cue: a bed, made, and a body-shaped hollow that has not filled in
decisions.cost: lie in it and you rest fully; you also stop, and the barrow prefers that

resolve.success: you see what the hollow is for and rest without lying in it — regain Grit, lose a Turn
resolve.failure: someone lies in it: they rest fully, and the barrow now counts them among what it keeps
resolve.orElse: press on tired: no rest, no cost, no attention

decisions.cue: a door held shut by nothing but the fact it has never been opened
decisions.cost: open it and something that had not changed, changes

resolve.success: you move it and it survives, just
resolve.failure: it does not survive, and the barrow notices what you cost it: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: squeeze past: one Turn and some skin

decisions.cue: a preserved thing blocking the way, which will not survive being moved
decisions.cost: move it and something here ends; leave it and lose a Turn

resolve.success: you open it having understood what changes
resolve.failure: something that had not changed, changes, and it was holding something back
resolve.orElse: leave it shut; the way on is longer

decisions.cue: food and water laid out, still good
decisions.cost: eating restores you fully and the barrow adds you to what it keeps

resolve.success: you eat and are restored entirely
resolve.failure: you are restored, and the barrow has added you to what it keeps: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: do not eat; you keep your Grit as it is

temptations.cue: a sealed jar holding one good year
temptations.benefit: open it to undo a wound entirely, once
temptations.standingDrawback: the year is spent in front of everyone, visibly

temptations.cue: a mirror showing the room a little younger
temptations.benefit: once, refuse a condition — the glass takes it
temptations.standingDrawback: the glass cracks a little each time, and so do you

temptations.cue: a child's shoes, unworn, in your size
temptations.benefit: you do not tire; ignore fatigue for a scene
temptations.standingDrawback: you have stopped ageing, and it shows in the wrong light

temptations.cue: a lamp still burning on three-century-old oil
temptations.benefit: light that never gutters
temptations.standingDrawback: nothing near it changes, including wounds you want to heal

temptations.cue: a flower that has not wilted
temptations.benefit: once, halt a condition where it stands
temptations.standingDrawback: it also halts something you wanted to finish

features: something here has been eaten, which should not be possible
a seal broken and the contents already spoiled
a clock stopped by hand — the pendulum caught and tied
one preserved thing removed, leaving a clean shape in the dust
a fire built recently, of furniture that was three centuries old
rot, in exactly one place, spreading

situations.doing: trimming a lamp that has never gone out
situations.onArrival: it will not stop, and speaks without looking up
situations.because: the task is what has kept it from ending
situations.offer: take the task from it, and it will finally rest — and tell you something first

situations.doing: a room is undoing your presence — footprints filling, dust returning
situations.onArrival: it works faster
situations.because: nothing here is permitted to change, including evidence of you
situations.offer: leave something deliberately and see whether it is allowed to remain

situations.doing: refusing to bleed, and frightened by it
situations.onArrival: they grab you and ask what is wrong with them
situations.because: the barrow has begun keeping them too
situations.offer: carry them out and the wound resumes; leave them and they stay perfect

situations.doing: setting a table for a meal that is always about to happen
situations.onArrival: they lay two more places
situations.because: the household was told to expect guests, and does
situations.offer: sit and eat — full restoration, and the barrow adds you to its inventory

situations.doing: waiting, exactly as instructed, and has been
situations.onArrival: it asks whether it is allowed to stop now
situations.because: nobody ever came back to release it
situations.offer: release it, and it gives you what it was guarding

situations.doing: repairing something that is not damaged
situations.onArrival: they set the work down and wait for inspection
situations.because: the standing order was to maintain, and there is nothing left to maintain
situations.offer: find them a genuine fault and they will fix a door you cannot

display.dangerLine: the barrow measures you against its host

institution: plinths along the stair, each holding a rival's finest thing
a gallery of gifts, none of them opened
cases arranged so the best is always further in
ritual: trophies mounted at a height that forces you to look up
a book recording who admired what, and for how long
a ribbon for every visitor who conceded the point
demand: an empty plinth, larger than the rest, waiting
a room that leaves you nowhere to stand but the centre
a case angled so you see yourself beside the prize
wound: a case of crowns, each slightly better than the last, all of them scratched
gifts defaced by whoever gave them
a plinth toppled, and the label kept
anchor: the piece every rival was meant to want, still under glass
a case holding one item and a great deal of space
a lock polished more often than the thing it guards

decisions.cue: an empty plinth, sized for something you are carrying
decisions.cost: leave a thing and the Host approves; keep it and they compare you unfavourably

resolve.success: you leave the offering with enough style that the Host counts you a peer
resolve.failure: your gift is judged and found wanting: +1 Bane, and they compare you aloud
resolve.orElse: keep everything: the next door stays shut, find the long way at one Turn

decisions.cue: a case of trophies and one obviously missing
decisions.cost: replacing it opens the next door; nothing else will

resolve.success: you work out what the gap held and what would satisfy it
resolve.failure: you fill it with the wrong thing and the Host notices the substitution
resolve.orElse: force the case: loud, roll the clock, and the display is ruined

decisions.cue: two ways on: one you must be invited down, one you may simply take
decisions.cost: the invitation costs an act of admiration; taking it costs their good opinion

resolve.success: the invitation is given and you go down honoured
resolve.failure: your admiration rings false: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: take the open way instead — free, and they think less of you for it

decisions.cue: a gift left for you, unopened, with your description on it
decisions.cost: opening it accepts the comparison; leaving it is a refusal, and noted

resolve.success: you open it and find something chosen for someone like you
resolve.failure: you open it and find it was not for you at all
resolve.orElse: leave it: a refusal, noted, and the Host is cooler from here

decisions.cue: a comparison invited — your gear against theirs
decisions.cost: engage and gain their favour; decline and be marked as beneath notice

resolve.success: you win the comparison and their favour with it
resolve.failure: you lose it publicly: +1 Bane and the Host addresses someone else
resolve.orElse: decline: you are beneath notice, which is its own kind of safe

decisions.cue: a display you could improve, or rob
decisions.cost: improving it opens the next door; robbing it opens all of them, badly

resolve.success: you improve the display and the next door opens for a benefactor
resolve.failure: your improvement is vandalism to them: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: rob it: every door in the barrow opens badly from now on

temptations.cue: the piece every rival was meant to want, still under glass
temptations.benefit: +1 die whenever someone must be impressed
temptations.standingDrawback: everyone who sees it wants it

temptations.cue: a ribbon awarded to whoever conceded the point
temptations.benefit: end one argument in your favour, once
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot decline a challenge while wearing it

temptations.cue: a gift, unopened, addressed to no one in particular
temptations.benefit: open it for exactly the thing you needed
temptations.standingDrawback: it was for someone, and they know

temptations.cue: a display case, small, with a good lock
temptations.benefit: anything inside is beyond casual theft
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever is in it is on show, always

temptations.cue: a plinth-plate engraved FINEST OF ITS KIND
temptations.benefit: once, make a thing you carry undeniably the best
temptations.standingDrawback: someone will want to test that

features: an empty case with the lock forced and the label left
a plinth pushed over, and nobody righted it
price marks chalked on the exhibits by someone practical
the best piece gone and a worse one moved into its place
a trophy defaced with a knife, thoroughly
sacking and rope left behind by people who meant to carry a lot

situations.doing: polishing a piece that is already flawless
situations.onArrival: they turn it toward you to be admired
situations.because: it was never admired enough while the Lord lived
situations.offer: admire it properly and they will show you the better one

situations.doing: weighing two trophies, unable to choose
situations.onArrival: they ask which is worth more, genuinely
situations.because: they can carry one and have been here an hour deciding
situations.offer: decide for them and take the other

situations.doing: a case is being restocked — items arriving in it, one at a time
situations.onArrival: a space clears, sized for something you carry
situations.because: the collection is still being completed
situations.offer: contribute, and the barrow counts you a benefactor

situations.doing: comparing every visitor against a portrait and recording the result
situations.onArrival: it begins comparing you
situations.because: the Lord required to know he was the finest thing here
situations.offer: lose the comparison deliberately and it relaxes entirely

situations.doing: setting out gifts nobody will open
situations.onArrival: they present one to you
situations.because: the giving was the point; the opening never was
situations.offer: accept without opening it, and they will carry your burdens

situations.doing: dusting an empty plinth with great care
situations.onArrival: it asks whether you have brought the replacement
situations.because: the finest piece was stolen and the post has been vacant since
situations.offer: give it anything at all and it treats you as the restorer of the collection

company.dangerLine: the barrow does not like it when people leave

institution: two sets of footprints in the dust, going in only
bedding laid for more than were ever buried
a coat-rack, full
ritual: chairs drawn up in a circle, all facing one seat
places set every evening for three hundred years
a table laid for more than were ever buried here
demand: hands, skeletal, holding other hands, the length of a hall
a doorway with the hinges taken off
a room arranged for a conversation that never ended
wound: a door barred from the inside, and the marks of it
scratches on the inside of a lid
a name called so often it wore into the wall
anchor: a keepsake still warm from being held
a chair kept empty and dusted
a second cup, always out

decisions.cue: one of the dead follows you and will not be told otherwise
decisions.cost: let it come and doors open; send it back and they close

resolve.success: you let it come, courteously — it opens doors and stays close
resolve.failure: it attaches: it will not be sent back, and it follows you out
resolve.orElse: send it back firmly: doors close, and the way on costs a Turn

decisions.cue: a chair drawn out, and a place laid, and time to sit
decisions.cost: sitting costs a Turn and buys the Host's goodwill entirely

resolve.success: you sit, are courteous, and leave — the Host's goodwill for the whole delve, one Turn spent
resolve.failure: you sit too long: +1 Bane, and they expect you at every table from here
resolve.orElse: walk past the setting: no goodwill, no obligation

decisions.cue: a door that will only admit one of you at a time
decisions.cost: splitting the party is exactly what this place wants

resolve.success: you find the order that gets everyone through without splitting for long
resolve.failure: you are separated: the party is in two places when the clock next fires
resolve.orElse: refuse to split: the door is not passed, one Turn to find another

decisions.cue: a hand, skeletal, held out to be taken
decisions.cost: take it and you are not alone; you are also not alone later

resolve.success: you take it and are not alone — once, something comes when you call
resolve.failure: you take it and are not alone later either, whether you call or not
resolve.orElse: do not take it: it is left held out, and the Host remembers

decisions.cue: a way on that only works if someone stays behind
decisions.cost: whoever stays is not alone, and that is the problem

resolve.success: whoever stays holds the way open and rejoins later, shaken
resolve.failure: whoever stays is kept: they rejoin at the ending, changed
resolve.orElse: nobody stays: the way is impassable, two Turns to go round

decisions.cue: an invitation to stay the night, meant sincerely
decisions.cost: accepting restores everything and costs a Turn and a Bane

resolve.success: you accept, rest fully, and the Host is yours for the delve
resolve.failure: you accept and the barrow counts you as staying: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: decline politely: no rest, no cost, slightly colder welcome

temptations.cue: a keepsake still warm from being held
temptations.benefit: once, someone comes when you call
temptations.standingDrawback: something else comes too

temptations.cue: a second cup, always set out
temptations.benefit: share it and gain an ally among the dead for a scene
temptations.standingDrawback: they expect to be included from now on

temptations.cue: a skeletal hand that closes gently on yours
temptations.benefit: you cannot be separated from the party by force
temptations.standingDrawback: nor can you leave one behind

temptations.cue: a folding chair, kept dusted
temptations.benefit: set it down and something friendly sits
temptations.standingDrawback: it follows you if you leave it

temptations.cue: a coat from a full rack, still shaped to someone
temptations.benefit: once, be treated as expected and welcome
temptations.standingDrawback: you are expected to come back

features: a bedroll, used, and not by anyone buried here
a chair dragged out of position and left where it was needed
two cups set out and one of them recently drunk from
a door tied open with a belt, so it could not close
someone has been counting the dead — tally marks by the entrance
a name carved beside another, joining them, badly

situations.doing: sitting in a circle, facing one empty chair
situations.onArrival: they shuffle round to make room for you
situations.because: the gathering may not end while anyone remains
situations.offer: sit, and they will answer anything while you do

situations.doing: holding a door open for someone who is not coming
situations.onArrival: it looks relieved and gestures you through
situations.because: it was told to wait and hold the door
situations.offer: walk through and it may finally follow — it will not leave you afterwards

situations.doing: talking steadily to a companion who is not there
situations.onArrival: they introduce you to the empty air
situations.because: the barrow does not like people leaving, and one of them did
situations.offer: play along and they will guide you; correct them and they stop speaking

situations.doing: a second set of footsteps is keeping pace with yours
situations.onArrival: they stop when you stop, close
situations.because: something attached itself in an earlier room
situations.offer: acknowledge it and it becomes useful; ignore it and it becomes insistent

situations.occupant: two of the Host, hand in hand
situations.doing: refusing to be parted to let anyone past
situations.onArrival: they look at you and do not move
situations.because: they were separated once and will not be again
situations.offer: find them a way to pass together and they open every door ahead

situations.doing: laying out a game for four
situations.onArrival: they look up and count you
situations.because: the fourth left and the game has never finished
situations.offer: play a round and they will tell you how the fourth got out

confession.dangerLine: the barrow is still listening for the right answer

institution: a kneeler worn through to the stone
a screen with a hole cut at the height of a mouth
benches facing one small window
ritual: written confessions, thousands, all in the same hand
a bell rung to begin, still roped
a queue of the dead facing a curtain
demand: a chamber where the echo answers differently than you spoke
a scale with a feather on one side and nothing on the other
a seat that will not let you rise until you have spoken
wound: a page torn from every book at the same place
a mouth chiselled off a statue
absolutions burned, and the ash kept
anchor: a confession nobody ever heard, sealed
a ledger of sins with the last page blank
a box that has only ever been opened once

decisions.cue: a screen, a kneeler, and a question you can hear being asked
decisions.cost: answer honestly and the way opens; lie and it opens anyway, differently

resolve.success: you answer honestly and the way opens, cleanly
resolve.failure: you lie and it opens anyway, onto somewhere else
resolve.orElse: go round: two Turns, and the question is still waiting

decisions.cue: a scale, one pan holding a feather, the other empty
decisions.cost: put something of yours in and it is weighed; walk past and you are not

resolve.success: you weigh something small and true, and pass
resolve.failure: you weigh something you needed: it is kept
resolve.orElse: walk past unweighed: the way on is longer by a Turn

decisions.cue: a book of absolutions with room for one more
decisions.cost: signing it forgives someone; it does not say who

resolve.success: you sign and someone long-accused is released
resolve.failure: you sign and the accusation transfers to you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it unsigned: nothing forgiven, nothing owed

decisions.cue: a door that opens to whoever admits something first
decisions.cost: whoever speaks pays; whoever stays silent owes

resolve.success: someone admits something and the door opens for them
resolve.failure: nobody speaks: the door stays shut and the silence is counted
resolve.orElse: force it: loud, roll the clock

decisions.cue: a question asked directly of one hero, by name
decisions.cost: answering costs privacy; refusing costs the way forward

resolve.success: you read the screen's angle and learn who has been here answering
resolve.failure: you learn nothing and your own voice is now in the echo
resolve.orElse: do not investigate: the room keeps its question

decisions.cue: a penance offered instead of a fight
decisions.cost: perform it and pass freely; it takes a Turn and it is humiliating

resolve.success: you perform the penance and pass freely
resolve.failure: the penance is refused as insincere: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: fight instead — the way is open either way, at a cost

temptations.cue: a confession nobody ever heard, sealed
temptations.benefit: read it aloud to unmake one accusation
temptations.standingDrawback: the thing confessed to becomes yours to answer for

temptations.cue: the feather from the scale, weightless
temptations.benefit: once, be believed absolutely
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot lie while carrying it, even usefully

temptations.cue: a fragment of stone worn through by knees
temptations.benefit: once, take a condition from someone else
temptations.standingDrawback: you keep every condition you take this way a little longer

temptations.cue: a splinter from the confessional screen
temptations.benefit: once, hear whether someone is lying
temptations.standingDrawback: they can tell you are listening for it

temptations.cue: a twist of ash from burned absolutions
temptations.benefit: once, erase a wrong you did here
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot remember it either, and it mattered

features: a confessional screen forced open from the wrong side
a page of absolutions torn out and burned separately
a kneeler moved to face a different way entirely
someone has answered the question aloud, and the echo has not settled
a knife left on the ledge where hands should rest
fresh ash in a place designed for keeping things

situations.occupant: one of the Host at a screen
situations.doing: hearing a confession from nobody, and nodding
situations.onArrival: it slides the panel and waits for yours
situations.because: it may not leave the box until someone is absolved
situations.offer: confess something true and it will absolve you — and tell you what it heard last

situations.doing: writing a confession they cannot finish
situations.onArrival: they ask you how to word it
situations.because: they think the barrow will let them go if they admit it properly
situations.offer: help them word it and they will hand over what they took

situations.doing: the room is repeating a confession, quietly, on a loop
situations.onArrival: it changes to your voice
situations.because: it keeps the last honest thing said in it
situations.offer: say something true and worse, and it will let you take the old one away

situations.doing: kneeling in a row, waiting to be heard
situations.onArrival: they turn, hopefully, toward you
situations.because: the confessor died and nobody replaced him
situations.offer: hear one of them, and the rest will stand aside for you permanently

situations.occupant: one of the Host with a scale
situations.doing: weighing small objects against a feather, all night
situations.onArrival: it holds out its hand for something of yours
situations.because: the Lord wanted to know he was not the heaviest thing here
situations.offer: give it something that matters and it will weigh a door open

situations.doing: reciting the same admission, over and over, getting no answer
situations.onArrival: it stops and asks whether that was sufficient
situations.because: nobody has ever told it yes
situations.offer: tell it yes and it will open the way it has been guarding out of gratitude

precedence.dangerLine: the barrow keeps its order, and you have joined the queue

institution: a stair too grand for the door it serves
the dead laid in strict order of rank, heads toward the centre
numbered flagstones, counting down
ritual: banners in sequence, each house a place further back
a herald's script with the order still marked
a queue that has not moved
demand: a corridor that will not let two walk abreast
a door only one person may pass at a time, and only first
a threshold worn on one side only
wound: rank-plates prised off and swapped
a name moved to the front by force, repeatedly
a procession that doubled back on itself
anchor: the crown worn first, and only once
a staff of precedence, laid down
a seat at the head of everything, occupied

decisions.cue: a corridor that will not let two walk abreast
decisions.cost: whoever goes first meets whatever is there first

resolve.success: you settle the order and whoever leads meets what is there, ready
resolve.failure: you argue in the corridor and something arrives while you do
resolve.orElse: send one scout: slow, one Turn, and they are alone

decisions.cue: a queue of the dead, and a way to step round it
decisions.cost: waiting costs two Turns; pushing in costs the Host's patience

resolve.success: you step round without breaking the order, and the Host allows it
resolve.failure: you push in: +1 Bane and the queue closes behind you
resolve.orElse: wait: two Turns, and the Host thinks better of you

decisions.cue: a door that opens only for the foremost of a party
decisions.cost: someone must be named first, aloud, and the others must accept it

resolve.success: someone is named first, aloud, and the door opens for them
resolve.failure: the naming is disputed and the door reads that as no answer
resolve.orElse: let the barrow choose: it picks the loudest, and remembers

decisions.cue: banners in strict order, and one you could move
decisions.cost: reordering them opens a way and insults everyone buried here

resolve.success: you reorder them correctly and a way opens
resolve.failure: you reorder wrongly and insult everyone buried here: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave them: the way stays shut, one Turn to find another

decisions.cue: a stair where the order of descent is visibly recorded
decisions.cost: whoever goes last is remembered as having gone last

resolve.success: you settle the order before you descend and the record reads as a party, not a rabble
resolve.failure: you descend in a scramble: whoever is recorded last is treated as least by the Host from here
resolve.orElse: descend however you like and accept the record as it falls

decisions.cue: a claim to settle: which of you the barrow should address
decisions.cost: settling it opens the way; refusing to settle it does not

resolve.success: the claim is settled and the barrow addresses one of you from now on
resolve.failure: it is not settled, and the barrow keeps asking, in worse places
resolve.orElse: refuse to settle: the way on does not open

temptations.cue: a small crown, sized for someone who never grew
temptations.benefit: +1 die when others must defer to you
temptations.standingDrawback: you must be addressed correctly or lose the benefit

temptations.cue: a rank-plate prised off something and pocketed
temptations.benefit: go first through any door the barrow guards
temptations.standingDrawback: going first is now expected of you

temptations.cue: a staff of precedence, laid down and not taken up
temptations.benefit: once, decide the order of anything, and be obeyed
temptations.standingDrawback: you may never be second while you hold it

temptations.cue: a herald's script with your name pencilled in
temptations.benefit: once, be announced as whatever you claim
temptations.standingDrawback: you must live up to it in front of the Host

temptations.cue: a numbered flagstone, prised up, number one
temptations.benefit: once, insist on going first and be obeyed
temptations.standingDrawback: you go first into everything from now on

features: banners pulled down and stacked without regard for order
a rank-plate prised off and dropped, still shiny where it sat
someone has walked the corridor the wrong way, scuffing one side
the queue disturbed — three of the dead pushed aside
a numbered flagstone lifted and not replaced
a seat at the head of the hall dragged back, as if to sit in

situations.doing: waiting to pass a door, in strict order, not moving
situations.onArrival: the queue opens a gap at exactly your rank
situations.because: the first in line is waiting for someone who never arrived
situations.offer: take the gap and go with them; take the front and they will remember it

situations.doing: reading out an order of precedence to an empty hall
situations.onArrival: it pauses and asks where you fall in it
situations.because: the list must be read in full before anyone may proceed
situations.offer: name your own place in the order and it will be honoured, exactly

situations.doing: each refusing to go through a door second
situations.onArrival: they both look at you to break it
situations.because: neither may be seen to yield
situations.offer: rule between them and the loser attaches to you as a lesser

situations.doing: prising number-plates off the flagstones
situations.onArrival: they freeze, then offer you one
situations.because: they worked out the order is what keeps the doors shut
situations.offer: take a plate and go first anywhere — the Host will hate you for it

situations.doing: a procession is passing through, unhurried, and you are in its way
situations.onArrival: it does not stop or go round
situations.because: it has right of way and has had for three centuries
situations.offer: stand aside and be counted courteous; join it and be counted one of them

situations.occupant: one of the Host with a herald's staff
situations.doing: announcing arrivals to an empty stair
situations.onArrival: it announces you, inventing a rank
situations.because: the post requires arrivals and there have been none
situations.offer: accept the invented rank and the barrow will treat you as it

factions.name: The Silent Host
factions.essence: still performing the ritual they were buried for

factions.name: grave-robbers
factions.essence: got in first and cannot get out

factions.name: the Barrow-Wardens
factions.essence: sealed this place and stayed to make sure

factions.name: things that moved in
factions.essence: neither know nor care whose tomb this is

features: a door that has been wedged open from the inside
a hole broken through a wall, recently, and not by you
water that has got in and taken three centuries to do it
a lamp still burning on oil that should be long gone
a collapse that has opened a way the builders never meant
grave-goods stacked with obsessive neatness
a floor mosaic worn only along one path
an alcove emptied in a hurry

decisions.cue: two ways on: one narrow and dark, one wide and announced
decisions.cost: the wide way is faster and the barrow hears it

decisions.cue: a sealed door, and a crack you could squeeze through
decisions.cost: the crack costs skin and a Bane on a failure

decisions.cue: something valuable, awkward to carry
decisions.cost: carrying it slows you and it is not yours

decisions.cue: a member of the faction, alone and not yet hostile
decisions.cost: talking costs time; not talking costs later

decisions.cue: a shortcut down, through water
decisions.cost: everything gets wet, including what burns

decisions.cue: a way back, still open
decisions.cost: leaving now means it will be worse when you return

temptations.cue: a courtier's mask, gold leaf over lime-wood, the mouth fixed in a small smile
temptations.benefit: the Host receives you as court
temptations.standingDrawback: while worn you cannot be recognised by name

temptations.cue: a signet, still warm
temptations.benefit: doors that answer to rank open for you
temptations.standingDrawback: the barrow's servants bring you their problems

temptations.cue: a hand-mirror that shows the room a moment behind
temptations.benefit: once per scene, see what was just here
temptations.standingDrawback: your reflection lags, and others notice

temptations.cue: a book of names, one line left blank
temptations.benefit: write a name and the Host obeys it once
temptations.standingDrawback: your own name is now in it

temptations.cue: a small crown, sized for someone who never grew
temptations.benefit: +1 die when others must defer to you
temptations.standingDrawback: you must be addressed correctly or lose the benefit

likeness.label: a portrait painted while they still had a face
likeness.function: the only place they can be seen

record.label: the one complete roll of the dead
record.function: the only place the name survives

seal.label: the signet that is still obeyed
seal.function: the only thing the household answers to

vessel.label: a sealed jar holding one good year
vessel.function: the only thing here that has not aged

ornament.label: the piece every rival was meant to want

token.label: a keepsake they would not be parted from
token.function: the promise that someone would stay

testament.label: a confession nobody ever heard
testament.function: the only account of what was done

regalia.label: the crown worn first, and only once

skirmish.avoid: they do not open hostilities on a guest

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: on a hit, a free Called Shot to freeze for a round

fight.avoid: the Ghoul goes for court dress first — send someone plain

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour and drains 1 max Grit

triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed in one place longer than it takes to search it
